name: Klaviyo, Inc.
business: Klaviyo sells a cloud B2C CRM platform (email, SMS, data, analytics, AI agents) to ecommerce brands from small businesses to enterprises worldwide.

events.what: Interim Executive Officer (director stepping into management)
events.from: Klaviyo director; ex co-CEO Workday and Eightfold.ai

events.what: Co-CEO alongside founder and co-CEO Andrew Bialecki
CFO Amanda Whalen steps down to advisory role (to 2026-11-16)

next_event.source: No 2026 Investor Day or framework update found in Baba corpus (lexical and hybrid search, fiscal 2026); last Investor Day 2025-09-25 (document_id 52797). Q3 2026 print (first with CFO Erica Smith) is the next checkpoint, date not confirmed.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Target is non-GAAP operating margin (excludes SBC); compared with VA consensus operating_income / revenue, which tracks the non-GAAP line (FY2025 VA 13.71% matches reported 13.7%). Longer-term 20% target has no year.

statements.quote: In the next three years, we are going to expand our operating margins from 12%, which is where they are today at the midpoint of our guidance for fiscal 2025, to 15%-17% by fiscal 2028.
statements.speaker: Amanda Whalen

statements.quote: Over the next few years, beyond fiscal 2028, we'll continue to drive structural improvements driven by AI, efficiency in our go-to-market motions, leverage on our platform in R&D, all of which position us to achieve that longer-term margin target of 20%.
statements.speaker: Amanda Whalen

statements.quote: We are revising our full year 2026 non-GAAP operating income guidance down to a range of $212 million-$218 million, with non-GAAP operating margin of approximately 14%. This amounts to a $10 million reduction from the midpoint of our prior outlook and includes $10 million-$12 million in costs associated with our Agency acquisition, as well as continued investment behind product innovation.
statements.speaker: Amanda Whalen

street.gap_assumption: Target midpoint 16.0% (15% to 17% non-GAAP operating margin by fiscal 2028) minus VA FY2028 consensus non-GAAP operating margin 15.90% (operating_income 348.0M / revenue 2,189.4M) = +10 bps. VA's own 'Operating margin' line shows 16.67% for FY2028, which would put the street above the midpoint. Calendar fiscal year, so VA labels equal company years. Either way the street sits inside the target range.
street.source: Baba data_financials summary and fundamentals consensus (Visible Alpha) cid 1005566; margins and gap via data_compute

evidence_of_progress.note: VA EBITDA margin yoy: 4QFY-2025 +868.7 bps, 1QFY-2026 +483.8 bps (VA has not loaded the Q2 2026 actual). Reported non-GAAP operating margin: Q1 2026 about 16%, Q2 2026 13.7%; Q3 2026 guided 10.5% to 11% and full-year 2026 cut to about 14% (from prior midpoint) on the Agency acquisition and product investment, with gross margin falling on SMS mix (Q2 non-GAAP gross margin 73.4%, down 3 points).

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: VA FY2028 consensus non-GAAP operating margin 15.90% sits inside the 15% to 17% fiscal 2028 target (10 bps below the midpoint; VA's own operating margin line shows 16.67%), and 12-month forward EBITDA revision is +8.0%.
verdict: Cheap and de-rated growth software, not a GXO setup: the dated margin target (15% to 17% by 2028) predates the co-CEO and new CFO and the street already models it, so there is no unproven gap; the catalyst is a founder plus co-CEO structure, not a replacement.
open_questions: Will new CFO Erica Smith (from 2026-09-01) reaffirm or reset the 15% to 17% fiscal 2028 target given the 2026 guide cut and SMS gross margin pressure?
Is the 68% drawdown about growth durability and AI disruption of email marketing rather than margin, which would make the margin lens the wrong one?
Does the co-CEO structure with founder Bialecki signal a later handover or a formal Investor Day in 2026 to 2027?
